Sample wording: adapt it to your own practice.
Design proposal and fee letter of {set:company}, dated {today}.
Dear {col:proposals.contact}, thank you for the chance to design your {col:proposals.project_type} project. This letter sets out our proposal and our fee.

Fee model: {col:proposals.fee_type}. Design fee estimate: {col:proposals.fee_estimate}, which is {col:proposals.fee_share} of your estimated FF&E (furniture, fittings and equipment) budget of {col:proposals.ffe_budget_est}. The service lines add up to {col:proposals.lines_total}.
The earliest start date is {col:proposals.earliest_start}. A retainer secures the start date and is credited against the first fee invoice. Prices are before any tax.
This proposal is valid until {col:proposals.valid_until}. To accept it, sign below and return this letter with the retainer.
Scope of services for a proposal
Scope of services of {set:company} for {col:proposals.contact}, dated {today}. Proposal {col:proposals.proposal_id}, {col:proposals.project_type}.
Stages: discovery and brief; concept design; design development; specification and approval; procurement; installation; styling and handover. Each stage ends with a written approval from you.
Fee model: {col:proposals.fee_type}. Fee estimate: {col:proposals.fee_estimate}. The fee includes the revision rounds shown in the terms; extra rounds are priced from our rate card.

Not included unless we agree it in writing: structural work, planning permission, items bought by you directly, and work outside the rooms in the brief. Anything extra is priced in a change order before it starts.
Your FF&E budget estimate is {col:proposals.ffe_budget_est}. Items are bought on our trade accounts and sold to you with a mark-up that we show on every purchase order.

Fee comparison of {set:company} for the sample project {col:feemodels.name}, dated {today}. Type: {col:feemodels.project_type}, {col:feemodels.rooms} rooms, FF&E budget {col:feemodels.ffe_budget}, about {col:feemodels.est_hours} studio hours.
Fixed fee: {col:feemodels.fixed_fee}. You know the fee in advance and it changes only through a change order.
Hourly: about {col:feemodels.hourly_fee} on our estimate. You pay for the hours used, so a project that moves faster costs less and one that grows costs more. A cap can be agreed.
Percentage of the FF&E spend: about {col:feemodels.pct_fee}. The fee follows what is bought, so it grows and shrinks with your budget.
The lowest fee for you is the {col:feemodels.cheapest} model. We will help you choose the model that suits your project and your wish for certainty.
Three package options for a budget

Three package options of {set:company} for {col:enquiries.contact}, dated {today}. Project: {col:enquiries.project_type}, about {col:enquiries.rooms_est} rooms. Your budget: {col:enquiries.budget_est}.
Essential: an FF&E budget of {col:enquiries.opt_ess}. Clean, durable choices with fewer custom pieces.
Refined: an FF&E budget of {col:enquiries.opt_ref}. More custom and trade-only pieces and a fuller lighting plan.
Luxury: an FF&E budget of {col:enquiries.opt_lux}. Bespoke joinery, premium fabrics and art, and the widest choice of vendors.
Your budget fits: {col:enquiries.fit}. Budget per room: {col:enquiries.budget_per_room}. We can phase the work if you prefer to start smaller.

Meeting on {col:consultations.date}: {col:consultations.kind}, {col:consultations.minutes} minutes, with {col:consultations.designer}. Contact: {col:consultations.contact}. Project type: {col:consultations.project_type}.
Outcome: {col:consultations.outcome}. Next step on {col:consultations.next_step_date}. Next step check: {col:consultations.step_flag}.
Days from the meeting to the proposal: {col:consultations.days_to_proposal}.
Notes of the meeting, the rooms visited and the points the client raised are written below.
Design brief summary of {set:company} for {col:briefs.contact}, dated {today}. Brief {col:briefs.brief_id}.
Rooms: {col:briefs.rooms}. FF&E budget: {col:briefs.budget}, which is {col:briefs.budget_room} per room.
Deadline: {col:briefs.deadline}, {col:briefs.weeks_left} weeks from the brief. Deadline check: {col:briefs.deadline_flag}.
Decision makers: {col:briefs.decision_makers}. Must-haves: {col:briefs.must_haves}. Style in plain words: {col:briefs.style_notes}.
Please check every line. Your signature approves the brief as the basis of the concept design.
Retainer invoice of {set:company}, dated {col:retainers.invoice_date}. Invoice for project {col:retainers.project_id}, client {col:retainers.client}.
Retainer amount: {col:retainers.amount}, before any tax. Due on {col:retainers.due_date}.
The retainer secures the start date of the project. It is credited against: {col:retainers.credited_against}. Fee type: {col:retainers.fee_type}.
After the concept stage starts the retainer is not refundable. Payment by bank transfer or card payment.
State of this invoice: {col:retainers.state}. Paid on: {col:retainers.paid_on}.

Dear {col:proposals.contact}, our proposal {col:proposals.proposal_id} for your {col:proposals.project_type} project is valid until {col:proposals.valid_until}, which is {col:proposals.days_to_expiry} days from today.
The fee estimate is {col:proposals.fee_estimate} ({col:proposals.fee_type}). After the expiry date the fee and the earliest start date, now {col:proposals.earliest_start}, may change.
If you have questions or want changes, please tell us. We can extend the proposal once if you need more time.

Dear {col:partners.contact}, thank you for the work you send us. So far you have sent {col:partners.leads} enquiries and {col:partners.bookings} became projects, with a contract value of {col:partners.value}.
Your last thank-you from us was on {col:partners.thank_you_date}. We value your trust and we always report back on the result of each project you send.
We would be glad to welcome you to the studio to see our latest projects.

Open Start and type your studio name and your own limits in the yellow cells: mark-up, fixed fee share, smallest fee, retainer share, target income per hour, reply hours and capacity hours.
Check Team, Clients and Projects. They hold the people, clients and projects that every other sheet looks up.
Fill Rate Card with your services, units, rates and minimum units. Cost and margin per unit fill in from your hour cost.
Fill Room Allowances with the FF&E allowance of each room type at three tiers. Every enquiry shows which tier its budget fits.
Log each enquiry on Enquiries, each first meeting on Consultations and each brief on Design Briefs. Replies, follow-ups and budget fit are checked for you.

Project timeline from type and start date
standard phase weeks for each project type give every phase end, each approval gate and the handover date from one start date
Client approval log with response speed
every approval is dated, answered or waiting, and each client gets an average days to approve and a slow flag
Phase slip impact on handover and trades
days late in one phase become a real handover slip, the cost of idle trade crews and the cost to the studio
Hours against fee with overrun forecast
hours logged against the estimate turn into a forecast at completion, an effective rate and the margin on a fixed, hourly or percentage fee
Project profit and margin per hour
fee, FF&E mark-up and trades mark-up less labour at hour cost show what each project really earned and per hour
Change order pricing and running scope total
extra items, rooms, hours and trades become a client price, an extra fee, the studio margin and the delay, with the approved total of the project
approved room budgets against the specified total show the variance, the reserve and what is over it
what part of an FF&E or hours overrun can still be billed for a fixed, hourly or percentage fee, and what the studio absorbs
Handover date forecast from the last delivery
last delivery date plus working days for installation, finishing fixes and the walk-through give the real handover date against the plan
the phase reached, fees paid and orders already placed give the fee earned, the refund or amount due and what cannot be cancelled
Client response speed and delay risk
average days to approve by client, requests waiting and the delay the gates ahead may cause

Project phases with hours and delays
One row per project phase with planned and actual dates and hours; hours variance, days late, the timing check and days to the phase end fill in by themselves.
One row per room with its approved budget; budget per sqm and the share of the project budget fill in by themselves.
Client approval log with response times

Change orders with the running scope total
One row per change order; the client, the running approved total of the project, days to approve and the share of the contract fill in by themselves.
Time entries by designer, project and phase
One row per block of logged time (the last 12 months); the value at the billing rate and the cost at the hour cost fill in by themselves.
One row per project with estimated, logged and billable hours; the share used, the value at rate, the overrun and the check fill in by themselves.
Margin per project and per hour
One row per project with fee billed, mark-ups and labour at hour cost; gross, margin, margin share, margin per hour and the target check fill in by themselves.
One row per project with the approved change orders, their value and extra hours; the share of the original contract and the FF&E budget gap fill in by themselves.
Milestones with due and done dates
One row per milestone (concept, drawings, handover) with owner and dates; days late and the state fill in by themselves.
Decisions with their effect on budget or schedule
One row per decision taken with the client; a revised-later flag shows when the same topic was decided again.
One row per site visit or measure with what was checked and any follow-up; the client, days since and the visit state fill in by themselves.
Project risks with score and next check
One row per risk with chance, effect, owner and next check date; the risk score, age and the status fill in by themselves.
Clients with terms and approval record
One row per client or prospect; the number of projects, contract value, open approvals and average days to approve fill in by themselves.
One row per client with a project; requests, average days to approve, the last approval and a slow flag fill in by themselves from the approval log.
One row per handover (done or coming) with the care guide, photos and walk-through; days after installation, steps done and the pack state fill in by themselves.
Standard weeks, share of hours and approval gate for each phase of each project type; the start and end week of every phase fill in by themselves.
Share of hours done at phase end
One row per Monday with active projects, late phases, approvals waiting and hours logged; hours per project, the week end and the phase check fill in by themselves.
One row per cancellation or pause with the reason and the fee kept; the kept share of the design fee and the weeks out fill in by themselves.
One row per team member and freelance specialist; active projects, hours in the last 28 days and utilisation fill in by themselves.
